fixture. MAY ONLY SHRINK. gate_mutation_fixture_check.py fails when an
entry here gains a fixture (delete the entry) and when an entry names a
gate the script no longer declares (the baseline outlived its gate).
Deleting an entry without giving the gate a fixture does not work: the
label lands straight back in the missing set.

Entries are CLASSIFIED, not described in prose alone: 'no fixture is possible' and 'no fixture was written' are different states and only one of them is work. Counting them by grepping the reason text would be the same defect this registry exists to retire.

_advisory_note: Five entries below are not outstanding work. A gate declared ADVISORY exits 0 on every verdict, so no input makes it reject and the CAN-FAIL direction is unreachable by construction. That is a property of the DECLARATION, not of the checker: each has a --strict or blocking mode. Recorded here rather than silently omitted, because 'no fixture is possible' and 'no fixture was written' are different states and only one of them is work.

_classes.outstanding: No fixture has been written. The declaration is driveable against a fixture tree, so this is work.
_classes.unreachable: No fixture is POSSIBLE as declared. The gate is wired ADVISORY or report-only, so it exits 0 on every verdict and no input makes it reject. Closing this entry means changing the DECLARATION, not writing a fixture.
_classes.per_cell_corpus: bash expands the declaration once per published cell, so the input judged is a corpus item rather than a tree a fixture can stand in for as written.
